newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy to help Albania rebuild shattered schools.
newsitem.headline: Italy to help Albania rebuild shattered schools.

text.p: Italy pledged on Thursday to help Albania to rebuild an education system devastated during a spree of lawless violence and said it planned to increase investments and cooperation in the Balkan state.

Italian Education and Technology minister Luigi Berlinguer, visiting Tirana, said his government would draft a long-term programme to strengthen education exchange programmes with Albania, especially among universities.

"We want not only to offer an emergency aid to schools and universities looted or ruined but also to launch long-term programmes which open tangible ways to cooperate between the two countries," he told a news conference
Berlinguer's delegation included officials from Italy's foreign and social ministries as well as the heads of several universities.
Albania was plunged into near-chaos when several get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes failed and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
The targets of the armed mobs included schools, universities and museums as well as military depots and food warehouses.

Berlinguer, the first Italian minister to visit Albania since Prime Minister Romano Prodi won support on Wednesday to send an Italian-led security force, said Italy wanted to promote the spread of Italian culture and systems to Albania.

"We want to deepen our culture and language ties to Albanian schools. We want to offer more scholarships to Albanian students and post-graduate scholarships. We also want to increase the number of accords between universities," he said.

"We have concrete plan in priority fields for education institutions and the damaged systems. We want to help Albanians get into Italian universities. We are interested in studying the territory, forest and mining sectors."

Italian is now the third most popular foreign language in schools behind English and French, but many Albanians understand Italian through watching Italian television programmes. Albania is as close as 70 km (45 miles) to Italy at some points.
Berlinguer also reaffirmed that Italy was determined to push ahead and help the Albanian people, saying a diplomatic row between the two countries was now considered closed.
It erupted after Italian Deputy Foreign Minister Piero Fassino said Albanian President Sali Berisha should resign, a remark that drew immediate Albanian protests.
"This problem does not exist anymore. Mr. Fassino himself sent a letter to President Sali Berisha, explaining how his quotes were misunderstood," Berlinguer said.
He said the Italian government would organise classes for more than 3,000 Albanian children now living in refugee centres in Italy after fleeing the turmoil in Albania.
